elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: Disputes are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Disputes are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any permitted fallback law.

elements.element: The designated courts correspond to the selected fallback law: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or London courts for the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates New York County courts rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or London courts.

result.reason: The rendered clause fully implements the preferred New York governing-law and exclusive-forum position. Restricting temporary injunctive relief to the selected New York courts avoids undermining exclusivity. The changes remove the conflicting Singapore provisions and make no unrelated substantive changes, although the remaining injunctive-relief sentence is somewhat redundant.
